title: Trump DOJ caught hiding information that would reunite families
description_short: Trump DOJ caught hiding information that would reunite families
description_medium: Lawyers trying to locate parents separated from their children at the border said the Justice Department turned over new contact information in December 2020 after months of requests. The data included phone numbers previously unknown to the search team. At the time, lawyers still did not know the whereabouts of 628 parents, and said the new information could help them find more families.
description_long: In December 2020, lawyers assigned to find families separated at the U.S. border said the Justice Department had finally given them new data after months of requests. A federal court filing described information from the Executive Office for Immigration Review, including phone numbers the legal team had not previously known. The team was working under an order from U.S. District Judge Dana Sabraw after the Trump administration separated parents and children in 2017 and 2018 without keeping adequate records to track them. NBC News reported that the number of parents whose whereabouts remained unknown had fallen from 666 to 628 as some families were identified. Lawyers said the new data could reduce the number further, though they had not had enough time to review it. The account establishes that contact details were provided and might assist searches; it does not say every family was located or reunited. The legal team’s report that data had been withheld for months describes a delay in the reunification effort, while the new information offered a possible route to finding additional parents.

preserved_fields.title: Trump DOJ caught hiding information that would reunite families
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump DOJ caught hiding information that would reunite families

notes: The account attributes the withholding claim to the lawyers’ court filing and describes the new data as potentially useful; it does not claim all families were found.

title: Trump: Mike Pence joins The Heritage Foundation
description_short: Trump: Mike Pence joins The Heritage Foundation
description_medium: Former vice president Mike Pence joined the Heritage Foundation as a distinguished visiting fellow in February 2021. The think tank said he would advise policy experts, give speeches and write a monthly column. Pence described Heritage as a flagship of the conservative movement, while its president said the organization had worked closely with Trump administration officials on policy during the preceding four years.
description_long: Mike Pence joined the Heritage Foundation as a distinguished visiting fellow shortly after leaving the vice presidency. The conservative think tank said he would advise its experts on public-policy issues, deliver a series of speeches and write a monthly column. Pence called Heritage a flagship of the conservative movement and said he was honored to work with the organization to advance conservative policies. Heritage president Kay C. James said the group had worked closely with Trump administration officials on policy accomplishments during the previous four years and welcomed Pence’s role in continuing that work. Pence’s appointment placed a former vice president in a public-facing policy role at an organization that had collaborated with the administration he served. The announcement described an advisory and speaking position; it did not establish that Pence held government authority or that the fellowship involved improper conduct. The entry documents his move into think-tank work and the organization’s stated policy aims after the Trump administration, rather than an allegation of wrongdoing.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Mike Pence joins The Heritage Foundation
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Mike Pence joins The Heritage Foundation

notes: The fellowship’s stated work was advising, speeches and a monthly column; the description does not infer misconduct from Pence joining the think tank.

title: Trump: New York AG joins Manhattan DA's Trump investigation
description_short: Trump: New York AG joins Manhattan DA's Trump investigation
description_medium: New York Attorney General Letitia James’s office announced that staff would assist Manhattan District Attorney Cy Vance’s criminal investigation of the Trump Organization. James’s office was already conducting a civil inquiry and said it had found evidence of a possible crime. The announcement described investigative cooperation, not a charge or finding against Trump.
description_long: In May 2021, New York Attorney General Letitia James’s office said staff members were assisting Manhattan District Attorney Cy Vance’s criminal investigation of the Trump Organization. James’s office had already been conducting a separate civil investigation and said it had found evidence of a possible crime. The Associated Press headline linked to this entry reported that two lawyers from the attorney general’s office were working with the district attorney. Their participation brought the state civil inquiry and Manhattan’s criminal probe into closer coordination, but the announcement did not itself charge Trump or establish that a crime occurred. The supplied account does not specify the conduct James’s office viewed as potentially criminal, identify the evidence it had found, or describe the investigation’s procedural status beyond the lawyers’ assistance. Those details are necessary to explain the basis and scope of the cooperation. The event can be described as an expansion of investigative coordination around the Trump Organization; it should not be treated as a finding of liability or guilt. The underlying allegation and later case outcome require an accessible report or docket to describe accurately.
